findings.title: First Nations primary-care attachment in B.C.
findings.public_summary: In 2017/18, 23.0% of First Nations people in the reported B.C. dataset were not attached to a regular primary-care provider, compared with 17.5% of Other Residents. This describes a difference in that population and period; it does not identify a single cause or show what changed later.
findings.what_was_measured: Age-standardized non-attachment to a regular primary-care provider in the source-defined First Nations and Other Residents populations.
findings.compared_with: 23.0% of First Nations people compared with 17.5% of Other Residents in 2017/18.
findings.what_it_does_not_establish: A current rate, a local centre or catchment result, a single cause, discrimination, or the experience of all Indigenous peoples.
findings.documented_context: This is a historical, province-wide administrative measure using the report's population and attachment methodology.
findings.caveat: A measurable disparity does not by itself establish discrimination or its cause.

findings.title: First Nations-led primary-care implementation in B.C.
findings.public_summary: B.C. reported 26,599 visits, 3,601 net-new attachments and 98.73 recruited full-time equivalents across the operating First Nations-led Primary Care Centres in its December 2025 reporting. These are implementation outputs, not a population-level measure of improved attachment or continuity.
findings.what_was_measured: Reported visits, net-new patient attachments and recruited full-time equivalents across operating First Nations-led Primary Care Centres.
findings.compared_with: Not a comparison-rate measure; these are reported implementation outputs for the current fiscal year as of December 2025.
findings.what_it_does_not_establish: Sustained attachment, continuity, reduced emergency-department or preventable-hospital use, improved patient experience, reduced travel burden, or causal effectiveness.
findings.documented_context: B.C. describes the centres as First Nations-led, team-based care that can include traditional wellness, mental-health, mobile and virtual supports.
findings.caveat: Implementation activity is not the same as a measured population outcome.

findings.title: Documented Indigenous primary-care barriers in Alberta
findings.public_summary: Alberta’s Indigenous Primary Health Care Advisory Panel documented barriers involving access, jurisdiction, transportation, infrastructure, workforce and cultural safety. These documented barriers help explain why access requires closer examination; they do not prove the cause of every health outcome.
findings.what_was_measured: A formal advisory-panel account of barriers identified in Indigenous primary health care.
findings.compared_with: Not a rate comparison or a quantified causal model.
findings.what_it_does_not_establish: The cause of every health outcome, a finding about every person or community, or that each barrier affects every setting in the same way.
findings.documented_context: The report provides a source-backed account of structural issues to investigate alongside measured outcomes.

source.title: Honouring Our Roots: Indigenous Primary Health Care Advisory Panel final report

findings.caveat: Documented mechanisms help frame a question; they do not by themselves prove causation.

findings.title: Alberta primary-care and navigation response
findings.public_summary: Alberta established Indigenous-led primary-care and patient-navigation funding after documented access concerns. Public reporting confirms funding, initiatives and first-year recipient reporting; it does not yet show whether access, continuity or experience improved.
findings.what_was_measured: Publicly reported funding programs, initiatives and first-year recipient reporting.
findings.what_it_does_not_establish: Whether access, continuity or patient experience improved, or whether the programs caused a change.
findings.documented_context: The Innovation Fund and Indigenous Patient Navigator Grant Program are intended to support Indigenous-led, culturally safe primary care and navigation.

suggested_follow_ups.title: Saskatchewan primary-care continuity and preventable hospitalization
suggested_follow_ups.research_question: Can Saskatchewan measure First Nations/comparator primary-care continuity and potentially preventable hospitalization?
suggested_follow_ups.why_it_matters: Saskatchewan has important First Nations outcome evidence, but an aligned public continuity/ACSC series was not located. Without aligned measures, public evidence cannot test the access-to-hospital-use link.
suggested_follow_ups.what_we_currently_know: Important First Nations health disparities have been publicly documented, while an aligned primary-care continuity and ambulatory-care-sensitive-condition series has not been located in the public record.
suggested_follow_ups.what_is_missing: An aligned Saskatchewan First Nations/comparator attachment or continuity and ACSC series.
suggested_follow_ups.evidence_needed: Governed, age-standardized, privacy-suppressed aggregate measures with population definition, numerator, denominator, method and linkage limits.
suggested_follow_ups.governance_considerations: An administrative Registered First Nations field is not all Indigenous people. Métis and Inuit require distinct appropriate approaches; aggregate availability would not settle governance or interpretation.

suggested_follow_ups.title: Saskatchewan medical-travel burden
suggested_follow_ups.research_question: What medical-travel burden is measurable for eligible First Nations patients in Saskatchewan?
suggested_follow_ups.why_it_matters: NIHB expenditure documents transportation activity, but not trip volume, distance, delay, cancellation, accommodations, escort use or continuity burden.
suggested_follow_ups.what_we_currently_know: Public program information confirms medical transportation as a covered benefit for eligible clients when medically necessary services are not available locally.
suggested_follow_ups.what_is_missing: A public privacy-safe account of trip, distance, delay, cancellation, accommodation, escort and completed-care measures.
suggested_follow_ups.evidence_needed: Privacy-safe aggregate operations measures and an eligible-population denominator where governance permits.
suggested_follow_ups.governance_considerations: Program eligibility is not a First Nations/non-First Nations comparator. Aggregate reporting should respect appropriate Indigenous data governance and suppression.

suggested_follow_ups.title: Alberta Indigenous primary-care investment outcomes
suggested_follow_ups.research_question: Did Alberta’s Indigenous primary-care investments improve access, continuity or patient experience?
suggested_follow_ups.why_it_matters: The programs were designed in response to documented access concerns. A public outcome series would help distinguish implementation from measurable improvement.
suggested_follow_ups.what_we_currently_know: Disparities and barriers were documented, programs were funded, initiatives were implemented and recipient annual reporting exists.
suggested_follow_ups.what_is_missing: Common public outcome indicators, comparable pre/post results and a population-level effect measure.
suggested_follow_ups.evidence_needed: Community-governed evaluation results or a public aggregate framework with baseline, intended population, period, method and limits.
suggested_follow_ups.governance_considerations: Community-led reporting may have governance or publication restrictions. Absence of a public outcome series does not show the programs failed.

suggested_follow_ups.title: B.C. First Nations-led Primary Care Centre outcomes
suggested_follow_ups.research_question: Did First Nations-led Primary Care Centres improve attachment and continuity in the populations they were designed to serve?
suggested_follow_ups.why_it_matters: Implementation data establish service activity but cannot measure sustained access improvement.
suggested_follow_ups.what_we_currently_know: B.C. documents centres, staff, visits and net-new attachments. It also reports a rapid formative evaluation and says additional community-led outcome indicators remain to be decided.
suggested_follow_ups.what_is_missing: A consistent, baseline-aligned catchment or intended-population outcome series for attachment or continuity.
suggested_follow_ups.evidence_needed: Community-governed, privacy-safe attachment and continuity measures for explicitly defined intended populations or catchments; emergency and preventable-hospitalization measures only where appropriate.
suggested_follow_ups.governance_considerations: First Nations and FNHA governance is central. A public outcome measure should be interpreted within the governance and population definition set by the appropriate partners.
